chunks: It was said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sayābah has a debt owed to him by a man who has died, and we spoke to him to absolve it, but he refused.”
So he said: “Woe to him! Does he not know that for him, with every dirham, there are ten if he absolves it; and if he does not absolve it, then he only has one dirham in place of one dirham?”

key_terms.دَيْنًا: a financial debt owed to someone
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a unit of money, here referring to the amount owed
key_terms.عَشَرَةً: tenfold reward in return for forgiveness
key_terms.مَاتَ: he died, indicating the debtor has passed away
key_terms.وَيْحَهُ: an expression of reproach and pity
key_terms.يُحَلِّلَهُ: to release or absolve him from the debt

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for forgiving the debt of a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teaches the virtue of forgiving a debt owed by a deceased person. He explains that waiving such a claim brings multiplied reward, whereas insisting on repayment yields only the original amount.
